messages.author: 01a10202e22a9666
messages.subject: matrixpls error message
parts:
Dear everyone
I'm learning matrixpls for pls-sem. I met problem.
The following is syntax.
-----------
data=read.csv("D:/r-SEM/data/data.csv")
price = c(0,0,0,0,0)
service = c(0,0,0,0,0)
atm = c(0,0,0,0,0)
cs = c(1,1,1,0,0)
cl = c(0,0,0,1,0)
cs_inner = rbind(price, service, atm)
cs_outer = list(1:4, 5:8, 9:12, 13:16, 17:20)
cs_mod = rep("A", 6)
matrixpls.res <- matrixpls.plspm(data, cs_inner, cs_outer, cs_mod,
                                 scaled=FALSE, boot.val=FALSE)
print(summary(matrixpls.res))

Next is a error message. please give me hint.

error in get_params(x = Data, inner = path_matrix, outer = blocks, modes = modes,  : 
  Invalid argument 'inner'. Must be a square matrix.
> print(summary(matrixpls.res))
Error in summary(matrixpls.res) : object 'matrixpls.res' not found
>

Best regards,

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: matrixpls error message
parts:
Your rbind command should cover all five of the composite proxies.  In this syntax, it covers only the first three.
--Ed Rigdon

Sent from my iPad

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: matrixpls error message
parts:
Hi

As Ed explained, the problem is that the inner matrix must be square, but your inner is 3 by 5. 

However, instead of working with the plspm compatibility function (matrixpls.plspm)I recommend that you use the matrixpls function directly. This way you can use lavaan model specification syntax, which will make your life a lot easier. See this example:

https://github.com/mronkko/matrixpls/blob/master/example/matrixpls-example2.R

Mikko
